name: Vega 1
first: First-ever balloon aerostat deployed in another planet's atmosphere (Venus, 1985); first spacecraft to carry science to two distinct solar-system targets
description: Soviet–ESA flagship of the Halley armada. Vega 1 launched 1984-12-15 with a Venera-lineage lander plus a first-of-kind ESA/CNES-built helium balloon that drifted in Venus's cloud deck at 54 km altitude for 46.5 hours, transmitting wind + temperature data via a 20-station global radio net. After dropping its descent module the bus used Venus gravity assist to redirect to comet 1P/Halley, achieving a 8890 km closest approach on 1986-03-06 — the first cometary nucleus encounter, and the position fix that ESA's Giotto used to navigate its own much closer Halley flyby a week later.

events.label: LAUNCH
events.note: Proton-K / D-1 lifts Vega 1 from Baikonur.

events.label: VENUS ENCOUNTER
events.note: Descent module separates + lands; balloon deploys at 54 km altitude for 46.5 hours.

events.label: HALLEY FLYBY
events.note: Closest approach to comet 1P/Halley at 8890 km — first cometary nucleus observation.
